chapters.title: The Soldier Who Would Not Carry a Gun

text: Desmond Doss went to war without a rifle.
That made men stare.
Doss kept going.
The Army did not know what to do with him at first.
A soldier who would not shoot seemed strange in a place built for fighting.
Other men wondered if he had freeze when danger came.
Doss did not freeze.
They would.
Doss stood apart in some ways.
He did not stand away from the men.
The day would come when those same men would call for help.
The ridge rose like a wall.
The men called it Hacksaw Ridge.
The Americans had to climb into danger, and Doss climbed with them.
The men went up ropes and ladders with the sound of war above their heads.
The air was filled with smoke, shouting, and gunfire.
Every man knew the top would be worse.
Doss carried medical supplies instead of a rifle.
Doss was putting them back into reach.
The order came to pull back.
The fight had gone bad.
He stayed on top of the ridge, alone in the danger, listening for voices that still needed help.
Doss found one wounded man and dragged him to the edge.
Then he tied the rope and lowered him down.
So he went back.
Night settled over the ridge, but the danger did not leave.
Enemy fire still cracked in the dark.
Men still groaned from the ground.
Some called for their mothers.
"Lord, help me get one more." Then he went back into the dark.
One more became many.
The men below could hardly believe it.
A man without a gun could still be one of the bravest men on the battlefield.
Doss kept serving even after the rescue night.
He had already done more than most men could imagine.
That was his kind of courage.
Later, Doss was wounded himself.
Even then, he thought of others.
He waited while another man was carried out first.
That was how he lived.
It climbed back into danger again and again.
Desmond Doss became a hero with empty hands.
No rifle.
On that ridge, mercy looked strong.
